gaps.lead: 'I may be late tonight,' my wife said.
gaps.sentence: My wife said ___ late that night.
gaps.explanation: may often backshifts to might: she might be late.

gaps.lead: Despite his injury, he finished the marathon.
gaps.explanation: in spite of + noun/-ing: In spite of his injury.

gaps.lead: Don't worry — the shops will still be open when you arrive.
gaps.explanation: Future simple with still: will still be open.

gaps.lead: You must sign the form in ink.
gaps.explanation: sign the form in ink → the form must be signed in ink.

gaps.lead: It wasn't necessary for her to cook — we ate out.
gaps.explanation: needn't have + participle = it wasn't necessary, but it happened; 'we ate out' shows the cooking served no purpose.

gaps.lead: The plane had just taken off when the warning light appeared.
gaps.sentence: The plane had ___ when the warning light appeared.
gaps.explanation: had just + participle = a very short time before.
